name: Resolution over one set of records: the hierarchy of section 2.5.10, defaults, requested types, negotiation, disclosure and the linkset

vectors.description: A serialised request with no linkType redirects to the model's default; the link is model information and the item record contributes only its own link.
The linkset for a serialised request carries the item anchor and the model anchor, each with its own links.
A variant-and-lot request unions the 01+22+10, 01+10, 01+22 and 01 levels, most specific first.
A lot-only request does not find a link registered against the variant and lot together.
A requested type registered at the lot level redirects to it.
Accept-Language fr picks the French refined default.
Accept-Language de matches no refined default, so the single default answers.
A requested type with two representations is decided by the Accept header.
A restricted link type requested by a public audience is not found; it is not disclosed by refusal wording either.
The same request from an authorised audience redirects, with the link flagged restricted.
Three product pages, one with no language declared and two contradicting Vietnamese: the one that makes no claim answers.
Two sustainability representations under an Accept of */*: neither is better, so the resolver answers 300 rather than choosing.
A requested type nobody registered is 404 with the available links beside it.
A GTIN nobody registered is 404 with nothing beside it.
A lot nobody registered walks up to the GTIN-level default, the walk-up the resolver standard section 2.5.9 requires and its test suite checks; the link is model information.
Over a set holding only the item record, the same request finds no record at its level or above: 404 where the standard requires a default. The set rule below refuses such a set.
The five records together: every GTIN they name has one public single default at the GTIN level, and no entity has two.
The item record alone: its GTIN has no default at the GTIN level, so a request for the GTIN or any lot under it has nothing to walk up to.

problems: GTIN 09521234000013 has no single default link at the GTIN level, so a request under it can have no default to walk up to (resolver standard section 2.5.9)

vectors.description: The variant, lot, variant-and-lot and item records without the GTIN-level record: refused for the same reason, however many qualified records there are.

problems: GTIN 09521234000013 has no single default link at the GTIN level, so a request under it can have no default to walk up to (resolver standard section 2.5.9)

vectors.description: The four qualified records with a GTIN-level record whose only defaults are refined ones (multi), which the record check admits: refused, because the GTIN has no single default for a request to fall back to.

problems: GTIN 09521234000013 has no single default link at the GTIN level, so a request under it can have no default to walk up to (resolver standard section 2.5.9)

vectors.description: The four qualified records with a GTIN-level record whose single default is restricted: refused, because a public request under the GTIN then has no default to walk up to.

problems: the GTIN-level default link of 09521234000013 is restricted, so a public request under it can have no default to walk up to (resolver standard section 2.5.9)

vectors.description: The five records with a second GTIN-level record carrying another single default: refused, because an identified entity has at most one single default across its records.

problems: 01:09521234000013 has 2 single default links across its records; an identified entity has at most one
